source_title: Hippo Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results - PR Newswire
source_excerpt:
SAN JOSE, Calif. , Oct. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Hippo Holdings Inc. (NYSE: HIPO ), a technology-native insurance platform reported net income of $9 million, or $0.33 per diluted share and adjusted net income of $20 million, or $0.74 per diluted share, for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.
Gross Written Premium of $498 million increased 60.1% over 3Q25
Revenue of $156 million grew 29.4% over 3Q25
Net income of $9 million compared to $98 million in 3Q25
Adjusted net income of $20 million (1) increased 9.3% over 3Q25
Combined Ratio improved 1 percentage point to 98.4% compared to 3Q25
Net Loss Ratio of 56.7% compared to 47.6% in 3Q25
CAT Loss Ratio of 6.5% compared to (0.3)% in 3Q25
Expense Ratio of 41.7% improved from 52.0% in 3Q25
Book Value per share of $17.62 up 3.8% from year-end 2025
(1) Non-GAAP financial measure; see "Reconciliation of Non-GAAP Metrics Financial Measures" below
"Hippo had a strong quarter, delivering a 98% Combined Ratio, a one-point improvement over last year, despite a 7-point headwind from more normalized CAT losses compared to none in the prior-year quarter. This helped generate a 9% increase in Adjusted Net Income over Q3 of last year to $20 million. On the top line, Gross Written Premium of $498 million was higher by 60% compared the prior year quarter, with expansion across all four of our main lines of business, Homeowners, Renters, Commercial Multi-peril, and Casualty. Net Written Premium grew 26% over last year to $149 million, " said Rick McCathron, Hippo President and CEO.
He continued, "These results reflect the foundation we've built: underwriting discipline, a diversified portfolio, and a program platform built for long-term partnerships. Even as the market softens, we've been able to grow while improving profitability, and we'll stay selective, writing more only where we believe the underwriting economics are attractive. That discipline supports our expectation of long-term profitable growth across the MGA and program space."

Net income of $9 million, or $0.33 per diluted share, compared to $98 million in Q3 of last year. The change was driven primarily by the $91 million net gain on sale of the home builder distribution network last year which more than off-set the improved operating performance.
Adjusted net income of $20 million, or $0.74 a diluted share, compared to $18 million in Q3 of last year. This quarter's results equate to a 17% annualized adjusted return on average stockholders' equity.
Gross written premium of $498 million for the quarter increased 60% year over year, up from $311 million in Q3 of last year. All lines of business delivered growth in the quarter, led by the continued expansion of Casualty and Commercial Multi-Peril (CMP) lines which were up 146% and 63% over last year, to $188 million and $108 million, respectively. The overall growth strategy is focused on improving underwriting profitability and reducing volatility, including through greater portfolio diversification. The overall portfolio on a gross written premium continues to become more balanced across perils with Casualty at 38%, CMP at 22% and Homeowners 23%.
Net written premium of $149 million increased by $31 million or 26% from Q3 of last year. Growth in net written premium lagged the growth in gross written premium as the fast growing lines, Casualty and CMP, also are the lines with the lowest retention levels. For the quarter, Homeowners' accounted for 50% of net written premium compared to 64% in the prior year quarter. The overall 30% net retention rate in the quarter was slightly lower than our full-year guidance of approximately mid-30s.
Revenue in the quarter of $156 million increased 29% from $121 million in Q3 of last year. The increase was primarily driven by higher net earned premium up 29% to $128 million, and increases in net investment income, commission income and service and fee income.
Net loss ratio of 56.7% compared to 47.6% in Q3 of last year. The change was driven by a more normalized level of CAT losses at 6.5% compared to no CAT losses in Q3 of last year, and the prior year period benefiting from 0.5% favorable prior year development. The net accident year loss ratio excluding CAT losses was 49.9% compared to 48.4% in Q3 of last year.
Expense ratio of 41.7% improved 10 percentage points over the prior year period driven by continued improvement of operating leverage, and continued focus on expense discipline. Most significant in driving this increased operating leverage was Net Earned Premium growth of 29% compared to the expense base growth of 12%, which accounted for 9 percentage points of the improvement.
Combined ratio of 98.4% improved 1 percentage point over the prior year period, as the expense ratio improvement more than off-set the more normalized CAT losses for the quarter.
Total Hippo stockholders' equity of $469 million was up 8%, from $436 million at year-end 2025.
Book value per share of $17.62, at September 30, 2026, was up 4% compared to $16.97 per share at year-end 2025.

Hippo Holdings Inc. subsidiaries include Hippo Insurance Services, Spinnaker Insurance Company, Spinnaker Specialty Insurance Company, and Wingsail Insurance Company. Hippo Insurance Services is a licensed property casualty insurance agent with products underwritten by various affiliated and unaffiliated insurance companies. Information about Key Operating Metrics/Non-GAAP Financial Measures
We define adjusted net income, a Non-GAAP financial measure, as net income excluding the impact of certain items that may not be indicative of underlying business trends, operating results, or future outlook, net of tax impact. We calculate the tax impact only on adjustments which would be included in calculating our income tax expense using the estimated tax rate at which the company received a deduction for these adjustments. We use adjusted net income as an internal performance measure in the management of our operations because we believe it gives our management and financial statement users useful insight into our results of operations and our underlying business performance. Adjusted net income does not reflect the overall profitably of our business and should not be viewed as a substitute for net income calculated in accordance with GAAP. Other companies may define adjusted net income differently.
We define diluted adjusted earnings (loss) per share, a Non-GAAP financial measure, as adjusted net income divided by the weighted-average common shares outstanding for the period, reflecting the dilution which could occur if equity-based awards are converted into common share equivalents as calculated using the treasury stock method. Diluted adjusted earnings (loss) per share should not be viewed as a substitute for diluted earnings (loss) per share calculated in accordance with GAAP. Other companies may define diluted adjusted earnings (loss) per share differently.
We define annualized adjusted return on equity, a Non-GAAP financial measure, as adjusted net income (loss) expressed on an annualized basis as a percentage of average beginning and ending Hippo stockholders' equity during the period. We use annualized adjusted return on equity as an internal performance measure in the management of our operations because we believe it gives our management and financial statement users useful insight into our results of operations and our underlying business performance. Annualized adjusted return on equity should not be viewed as a substitute for return on equity calculated in accordance with GAAP. Other companies may define annualized adjusted return on equity differently.
We define tangible book value per share, a Non-GAAP financial measure, as total stockholders' equity, less intangible assets and capitalized internal software, divided by the outstanding number of shares of our common stock at the end of the relevant period. Our definition of tangible book value per share may not be comparable to that of other companies, and it should not be viewed as a substitute for book value per share calculated in accordance with GAAP. We use tangible book value per share internally to evaluate changes from period to period in book value per share exclusive of changes in intangible assets.
These Non-GAAP financial measures are in addition to, and not a substitute for, or superior to, measures of financial performance prepared in accordance with GAAP and should not be considered as an alternative to net income, operating income or any other performance measures derived in accordance with GAAP. Reconciliations of these Non-GAAP financial measures to their most directly comparable GAAP counterpart is included above. We believe that these non-GAAP measures of financial results provide useful supplemental information to investors about Hippo.
The Company is unable to provide a reconciliation of Adjusted Net Income (Loss) to Net Income (Loss), its most directly comparable GAAP financial measure, on a forward-looking basis without unreasonable effort, because items that impact this GAAP financial measure are not within the Company's control and/or cannot be reasonably predicted. These items may include, but are not limited to, predicting forward-looking share-based compensation. Such information may have a significant, and potentially unpredictable, impact on the Company's future financial results.
